get.summary: Read the App hook and recent Delivery results.
get.description: Reads the configured URL and the latest page of the existing GitHub Delivery log, scoped to this installation and repository. Empty results establish no reachability. Does not poll Events or advance the cursor. Safe metadata only; no secrets or payloads.

parameters.name: organization
parameters.description: The name of the Organization the records belong to.

200.description: Configuration and observed Delivery results, not a reachability promise.

put.summary: Set only the GitHub App's webhook URL.
put.description: Uses the supplied public HTTPS base or the deployment webhook base. Preserves the secret, subscriptions and polling cursor. Refuses retired or shared Apps and unfinished secret rotation. GitHub acknowledgement says configuration changed, never that a Delivery reached kestrel. An unanswered update may have landed: inspect before retrying. A persisted pending_url serializes conflicting URL/secret maintenance until retrying the same base is acknowledged; retirement clears it.

parameters.name: organization
parameters.description: The name of the Organization the records belong to.

200.description: The Integration at its new revision; polling continues.

post.summary: Rotate the webhook secret of a GitHub Integration's App.
post.description: kestrel makes the replacement and saves it sealed before GitHub is asked, so from then on a delivery signed with either the previous or the replacement secret is accepted. It then sets the replacement as the App's webhook secret and, once GitHub acknowledges that, the replacement becomes the only secret. When GitHub does not acknowledge it, the rotation stays unfinished: it is the Integration's `webhook_secret_rotation`, and the refusal offers to resume it. Polling carries on throughout. Refused, saving nothing, for a generic webhook, an Integration that holds no webhook secret, a retired one, one whose App another Integration that is not retired also signs as (in any Organization, which the refusal does not name), one decided against an older revision, or one already rotating. The secret is never returned.

parameters.name: organization
parameters.description: The name of the Organization the records belong to.

post.description: Sets the same saved replacement as the App's webhook secret again, since GitHub masks the secret it reads back and only its acknowledgement shows the change took. Once GitHub acknowledges it, the replacement becomes the only secret. Resuming an Integration with no rotation under way changes nothing; a retired one has none, because retirement erased both secrets. Refused, leaving the rotation unfinished, when GitHub does not acknowledge the change or another Integration that is not retired now signs as the same App.

parameters.name: organization
parameters.description: The name of the Organization the records belong to.

200.description: The Integration, its rotation finished or none under way.
